then the delegate who reconsiders the decision must be a person who:
was not involved in making the decision; and
occupies a position that is senior to that occupied by any person involved in making the decision.
The reviewer of a reviewable decision relating to tuition protection may reconsider the decision if the reviewer is satisfied that there is sufficient reason to do so.
The reviewer may reconsider the decision even if:
an application for reconsideration of the decision has been made under section 187D; or
the decision has been confirmed, varied or set aside under section 187D and an application has been made under section 187E for review of the decision.
After reconsidering the decision, the decision-maker must:
confirm the decision; or
vary the decision; or
set the decision aside and substitute a new decision.
(4) The reviewer’s decision (the decision on review) to confirm, vary or set aside the decision takes effect:
on the day specified in the decision on review; or
if a day is not specified—on the day on which the decision on review was made.
The reviewer must give written notice of the decision on review to the person to whom that decision relates.
The notice:
must be given within a reasonable period after the decision on review is made; and
must contain a statement of the reasons for the reviewer’s decision on review.
Note: Section 266 of the Administrative Review Tribunal Act 2024 requires the person to be notified of the person’s review rights.

section.heading: Reconsideration of reviewable decisions on request

content.p: A person whose interests are affected by a reviewable decision relating to tuition protection may request the reviewer to reconsider the decision.

The person’s request must be made by written notice given to the reviewer within 28 days, or such longer period as the reviewer allows, after the day on which the person first received notice of the decision.
The notice must set out the reasons for making the request.
After receiving the request, the reviewer must reconsider the decision and:
confirm the decision; or
vary the decision; or
set the decision aside and substitute a new decision.
Despite subsection (4), the reviewer is not required to reconsider the decision if:
the decision was made under paragraph 62J(2)(b); and
the person gave notice in writing, under paragraph 62J(8)(c), that the person would not seek reconsideration of the decision.
(6) The reviewer’s decision (the decision on review) to confirm, vary or set aside the decision takes effect:
on the day specified in the decision on review; or
if a day is not specified—on the day on which the decision on review was made.
The reviewer must give the person written notice of the decision on review.
The notice:
must be given within a reasonable period after the decision on review is made; and
must contain a statement of the reasons for the reviewer’s decision on review.
The reviewer is taken to have confirmed the decision if the reviewer does not give notice of a decision to the person within 45 days after receiving the person’s request.
Note: Section 266 of the Administrative Review Tribunal Act 2024 requires the person to be notified of the person’s review rights.

An application may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for the review of a reviewable decision relating to tuition protection that has been confirmed, varied or set aside under section 187C or 187D.
Despite subsection (1), an application cannot be made for the review of a decision made under paragraph 62J(2)(a) or (b) (about suitable replacement courses).
Subdivision A—Restriction on disclosure or use of information

section.heading: Offence of unauthorised disclosure or use of information

content.p: A person commits an offence if:
the person obtains higher education information in the person’s capacity as an entrusted person; and
the person:
discloses the information to another person; or
uses the information.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years.
Exceptions
Subsection (1) does not apply if:

(a) the disclosure or use is made for the purposes of this Act or the Education Services for Overseas Students Act 2000, or otherwise in connection with the performance of the person’s duties as an entrusted person; or
the disclosure or use is required or authorised by or under a law of the Commonwealth or a State or Territory.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to a matter in subsection (2) (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).
Subsection (1) does not apply if the regulated entity in respect of whom the higher education information relates has consented, in writing, to the disclosure or use.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to a matter in subsection (3) (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).
Subdivision B—Information sharing

section.heading: Disclosing information about breaches of regulatory requirements

content.p: TEQSA may disclose the kinds of higher education information referred to in subsection (2) to:
a person who holds any office or appointment under a law of the Commonwealth, or under a law of a State or Territory; or
(b) a member, or special member, of the Australian Federal Police (within the meaning of the Australian Federal Police Act 1979); or
a member of the police force, or police service, of a State or Territory; or
an employee:
of a Commonwealth authority or of a State or Territory authority; and
of a kind specified in the Information Guidelines for the purposes of this section; or
(e) in the case of a registered provider (within the meaning of the Education Services for Overseas Students Act 2000)—the TPS Director, within the meaning of that Act; or
a regulatory authority of another country that has responsibility relating to the quality or regulation of higher education.
The kinds of higher education information are as follows:
(a) information that relates to an offence, or possible offence, against this Act, this Act’s associated provisions or the Education Services for Overseas Students Act 2000;
information that relates to a contravention, or possible contravention, of:
this Act; or
(ii) the Education Services for Overseas Students Act 2000; or
(iii) the Higher Education Support Act 2003; or
legislative instruments made under any of those Acts.

section.heading: Disclosing information about proposed cancellations of registration

content.p: TEQSA may advise the Minister of a State or Territory responsible for higher education if:
TEQSA has serious concerns about a registered higher education provider for whom an accredited course is being provided in the State or Territory; or
TEQSA proposes to cancel the registration of a registered higher education provider for whom an accredited course is being provided in the State or Territory.
If TEQSA advises the Minister of the State or Territory under subsection (1), TEQSA may also advise:
a person who holds any office or appointment under a law of the Commonwealth, or under a law of the State or Territory concerned; or
employees of the Commonwealth of a kind specified in regulations made for the purposes of this paragraph; or
employees of the State or Territory of a kind specified in regulations made for the purposes of this paragraph.

section.heading: Disclosing information to Tertiary Admission Centres

content.p: TEQSA may advise a Tertiary Admission Centre if:
TEQSA cancels the accreditation of a course of study; or

TEQSA imposes a condition on the registration of a higher education provider that restricts the number of students that may enrol in a particular course of study accredited in relation to the provider; or
TEQSA cancels the registration of a registered higher education provider.

section.heading: Disclosing information to the Minister and Department

content.p: For the purposes of administering laws relating to higher education, TEQSA may disclose information covered by subsection (2) to:
the Minister; or
(b) a person employed by the Minister under the Members of Parliament (Staff) Act 1984; or
the Secretary; or
the Higher Education Tuition Protection Director; or
an APS employee in the Department.
This subsection covers the following information:
higher education information;
(b) information, relating to a regulated entity, that is obtained by TEQSA, that relates to TEQSA’s functions and that is personal information (within the meaning of the Privacy Act 1988).

section.heading: Disclosing information to professional bodies etc.

content.p: TEQSA may disclose higher education information to a body responsible for the regulation of an occupation in a State or Territory.

section.heading: Disclosing information to certain government bodies etc.

content.p: TEQSA may disclose higher education information to:
a Commonwealth authority, or a State or Territory authority, if:
the authority is of a kind specified in the Information Guidelines for the purposes of this section; and
TEQSA is satisfied that the disclosure is necessary to enable or assist the authority to perform or exercise any of the authority’s functions or powers; or
a Royal Commission.

section.heading: Disclosing information to National Student Ombudsman

content.p: TEQSA may disclose higher education information and personal information to the National Student Ombudsman if the disclosure is for the purposes of assisting the National Student Ombudsman to perform its functions or duties or exercise its powers.

section.heading: Disclosing information under international cooperative arrangements

content.p: TEQSA may disclose higher education information to a regulatory authority of another country if:
cooperative arrangements exist with that other authority or country that relate to the assessment or regulation of higher education; and
the release of the information is consistent with those arrangements.
Disclosure
TEQSA may disclose higher education information to a person referred to in subsection (3) for the purposes of research relating to the provision of higher education, including research relating to:
quality assurance; or
planning the provision of higher education.
However, if the information was provided by a regulated entity, TEQSA may disclose the information under subsection (1) only if the entity has consented, in writing, to that disclosure.
Persons to whom information may be disclosed
For the purposes of subsection (1), the persons are the following:
a person who is employed or engaged by a higher education provider;
a person who is employed or engaged by a body determined in an instrument under subsection (4).
TEQSA may, by legislative instrument, determine a body for the purposes of paragraph (3)(b).
TEQSA may disclose higher education information to a person if:
the person has made a complaint to TEQSA relating to a regulated entity’s compliance with:
this Act; or
(ii) the Education Services for Overseas Students Act 2000; or
a legislative instrument under either of those Acts; and
TEQSA is satisfied that the information relates to the matter the subject of the complaint.
TEQSA may disclose to the public higher education information that relates to anything done, or omitted to be done, under this Act.
Paragraph 192(1)(d) and sections 193, 194, 195, 195A, 195B and 196 do not apply to national security information.
Subdivision C—Higher education student records

section.heading: Higher education student records to be provided to TEQSA

content.p: If:
an entity that is a registered higher education provider has effectively ceased to operate; or
an entity’s registration as a registered higher education provider is cancelled;

TEQSA may, by written notice given to a person who is, or was, an executive officer of the entity, require the person to provide to TEQSA a copy of such of the higher education student records relating to the entity as are specified in the notice within the period specified in the notice.
The period specified in the notice must be at least 14 days after the notice is given.
Offence
A person commits an offence if:
the person is given a notice under subsection (1); and
the person possesses or controls the higher education student records specified in the notice; and
the person fails to comply with the notice.
Penalty: 150 penalty units.
Civil penalty
A person contravenes this subsection if:
the person is given a notice under subsection (1); and
the person possesses or controls the higher education student records specified in the notice; and
the person fails to comply with the notice.
Civil penalty: 300 penalty units.

section.heading: TEQSA may request higher education student records

content.p: If:
either:
an entity that is a registered higher education provider has effectively ceased to operate; or
an entity’s registration as a registered higher education provider is cancelled; and
(b) TEQSA considers that a person (the holder) may hold higher education student records relating to the entity; and
the holder is not a person who is, or was, an executive officer of the entity;
TEQSA may, by notice in writing, request the holder to provide to TEQSA a copy of such of those records as are specified in the notice.

section.heading: Provision of higher education student records to another registered higher education provider

content.p: If:
(a) a person (the student) is enrolled in an accredited course provided by an entity (the first entity) that is a registered higher education provider; and
(b) the student transfers to another registered higher education provider (the second entity);
then:
the student may request the first entity to provide to the second entity a copy of the higher education student records relating to the student; or
the second entity may request, in writing, the first entity to provide to the second entity a copy of the higher education student records relating to the student.

section.heading: TEQSA’s management of higher education student records

content.p: TEQSA may provide a copy of a higher education student record it holds to a registered higher education provider if:
the person to whom the record relates has enrolled, or is seeking to enrol, in an accredited course provided by the provider and the person requests TEQSA, in writing, to provide the copy; or

with the consent of the person to whom the record relates, the provider requests TEQSA, in writing, to provide the copy because that person has enrolled, or is seeking to enrol, in an accredited course provided by the provider.

If the operation of section 197AA would result in an acquisition of property from a person otherwise than on just terms, the Commonwealth is liable to pay a reasonable amount of compensation to the person.

If the Commonwealth and the person do not agree on the amount of the compensation, the person may institute proceedings in the Federal Court for the recovery from the Commonwealth of such reasonable amount of compensation as the court determines.

division.heading: Management of academic cheating services information

section.heading: Offence of unauthorised disclosure or use of academic cheating services information

content.p: A person commits an offence if:
the person obtains academic cheating services information in the person’s capacity as an entrusted person; and
the person:
discloses the information to another person; or
uses the information.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years.
Exception
Subsection (1) does not apply if:

(a) the disclosure or use is made for the purposes of this Act or the Education Services for Overseas Students Act 2000, or otherwise is in connection with the performance of the person’s duties as an entrusted person; or
the disclosure or use is authorised by section 197B.
Note: A defendant bears an evidential burden in relation to a matter in subsection (2) (see subsection 13.3(3) of the Criminal Code).

section.heading: Authorised disclosure and use of academic cheating services information

content.p: Disclosing etc. information relating to providers of academic cheating services

TEQSA may disclose or use academic cheating services information if the disclosure or use is of information that a person provides, or is reasonably suspected by TEQSA of providing, an academic cheating service.
Disclosing information relating to users of academic cheating services
TEQSA may disclose academic cheating services information to a higher education provider if:
the disclosure is of information that a person has used, or is reasonably suspected by TEQSA of using, an academic cheating service; and
TEQSA knows, or reasonably suspects, that the person is or has been enrolled in a course of study with the higher education provider.
TEQSA may disclose academic cheating services information to a regulatory authority of another country if:
cooperative arrangements exist with that authority or country that relate to the regulation of higher education; and
the disclosure is consistent with those arrangements.
A person may disclose academic cheating services information to TEQSA to assist TEQSA in performing its functions under paragraph 134(1)(c), (da) or (j).
Section 197B does not apply to national security information.

part.heading: National Register of Higher Education Providers

section.heading: National Register of Higher Education Providers

content.p: TEQSA must establish and maintain a register of:
registered higher education providers; and
each entity that was a registered higher education provider and whose registration has been cancelled other than because of a reason set out in the Register Guidelines; and
authorised offshore providers; and
each entity that was an authorised offshore provider and whose authorisation has been cancelled other than because of a reason set out in the Register Guidelines.
The register is to be known as the National Register of Higher Education Providers.
The Register Guidelines may set out details that TEQSA must enter on the Register in respect of each registered higher education provider.
Subsection (3) does not prevent TEQSA from entering other details on the Register in respect of a registered higher education provider.
The Register is to be made available for inspection on the internet.
TEQSA may, by writing, delegate any or all of TEQSA’s functions and powers to:
a Commissioner; or
the Chief Executive Officer; or
a member of the staff of TEQSA who holds the classification of APS Executive Level 1 or higher, or an equivalent classification.
Note 1: This subsection extends, for example, to TEQSA’s functions and powers under the Education Services for Overseas Students Act 2000.
Note 2: TEQSA may also subdelegate powers delegated to TEQSA under section 170 of the Education Services for Overseas Students Act 2000.
Subsection (1) does not apply to a power to make, vary or revoke a legislative instrument.
In exercising functions or powers under a delegation under section 199, the delegate must comply with any written directions of TEQSA.

The Secretary may, in writing, delegate all or any of the Secretary’s functions or powers under this Act (other than paragraph 134(1)(i)) to an APS employee who holds or performs the duties of an APS Level 6 position, or an equivalent or higher position, in the Department.

The Secretary may, in writing, delegate the Secretary’s functions or powers under the Regulatory Powers Act as it applies in relation to Part 5A of this Act, to an SES employee, or an acting SES employee, in the Department.
Before delegating a function or power under subsection (1) or (2), the Secretary must have regard to:

if the function or power is delegated to an APS employee holding, occupying, or performing the duties of, a specified office or position—whether the office or position is sufficiently senior for the employee to perform the function or exercise the power; or
otherwise—whether the employee has appropriate qualifications or expertise to perform the function or duty or exercise the power.
In performing functions or exercising powers under a delegation under subsection (1) or (2), the delegate must comply with any directions of the Secretary.
The Minister may, in writing, delegate all or any of the Minister’s functions or powers under Part 5A to the Secretary.
Note: Sections 34AA to 34A of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901 contain provisions relating to delegations.
In performing functions or exercising powers under a delegation under subsection (1), the Secretary must comply with any directions of the Minister.

section.heading: Protection from criminal or civil actions

content.p: No action, suit or proceeding (whether criminal or civil) lies against a protected person in relation to anything done, or omitted to be done, in good faith by the person:
in accordance, or purportedly in accordance, with this Act; or
in the performance, or purported performance, of TEQSA’s functions; or
in the exercise, or purported exercise, of TEQSA’s powers.
Note: This section extends to, for example, a thing done in good faith in accordance with a delegation under section 199.
(2) The protected persons are as follows:
the Minister;
a Commissioner;
a member of the staff of TEQSA;
a Commonwealth authority;
a person who holds any office or appointment under a law of the Commonwealth;
a person performing a service for TEQSA.
The Minister must, before 1 January 2016, cause a review to be started of the impact on the higher education sector of this Act.

section.heading: Review of operation of tuition protection

content.p: Before 1 July 2021, the Minister must commence a review of the operation of Part 5A (about tuition protection).

Note: The review must be conducted at the same time as a review of the operation of Parts 5 and 5A of the Education Services for Overseas Students Act 2000, Parts 5-1A and 5-1B of the Higher Education Support Act 2003 and Parts 5A and 5B of the VET Student Loans Act 2016.
The Minister must cause to be prepared a report of a review under subsection (1).
The Minister must cause a copy of the report to be tabled in each House of the Parliament within 15 sitting days of that House after the completion of the report.

required or permitted by the corresponding provision mentioned in the third column of the table to be provided; or
necessary or convenient to be provided for carrying out or giving effect to that provision.

section.heading: Use of Australian domain names with the word “university” etc.

content.p: A person must not use a domain name:
with either:
the word “university” in the domain name; or
a word or expression, that has the same or a similar meaning to the word “university” and that is determined in an instrument under subsection (3), in the domain name; and
where the domain name includes an Australian top-level domain;
unless there is an approval in force under subsection (4) in relation to the person’s use of that domain name.
Scope of prohibition
Subsection (1) applies in relation to a person’s use of a domain name on or after the commencement of this section if:
the licence for the use of that domain name was issued on or after that commencement; and
no licence for the use of that domain name had been issued before that commencement to the licensee of the licence referred to in paragraph (a).
List of words or expressions
The Minister may, by legislative instrument, determine words or expressions for the purposes of subparagraph (1)(a)(ii).
Approval of use of domain names
The Minister may, in writing, approve a person’s use of a specified domain name. The Minister may give an approval on the Minister’s own initiative or on application.
The Minister must give a copy of the approval to:
the person; and
the licensor that issues licences for the use of a domain name to which paragraphs (1)(a) and (b) apply.
An approval under subsection (4) comes into force at the time it is given.
If a person makes an application for an approval and the Minister refuses to give the approval, the Minister must give written notice of the refusal and of the reasons for the refusal to:
the person; and
the licensor that issues licences for the use of a domain name to which paragraphs (1)(a) and (b) apply.
In deciding whether or not to give an approval under subsection (4), the Minister must have regard to:
whether the person is a registered higher education provider; and
the matters determined in an instrument under subsection (10).
Subsection (8) does not limit the matters to which the Minister may have regard.
The Minister must, by legislative instrument, determine matters for the purposes of paragraph (8)(b).
Licence details to be given to the Minister

The Minister may, in writing, request the licensor that issues licences for the use of a domain name to which paragraphs (1)(a) and (b) apply to give the Minister the following details in relation to the period specified in the request:
the name of each person to whom such a licence has been issued;
the domain name covered by the licence;
contact details for the person to the extent known by the licensor.
The licensor must comply with a request under subsection (11).
Delegation
The Minister may, in writing, delegate the Minister’s functions and powers under this section (except subsections (3) and (10)) to an SES employee, or acting SES employee, in the Department.
Approval not a legislative instrument
An approval under subsection (4) is not a legislative instrument.
The Governor-General may make regulations prescribing matters:
required or permitted by this Act to be prescribed; or
necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Act.
